SMTO-EXE-0066 — SMTO couldn't carry out that desktop request as asked

GUID: 5974824f-3422-539a-982c-eba4bff94c05
Slug: desktop-invalid-request
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO tried to work with apps or windows on the Gateway computer, but the request had missing or wrong details, or asked for something the Desktop skill doesn't allow. Nothing was done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Rephrase your request in the conversation, naming the exact app or window and what to do with it: open, switch to, close, move, resize, minimize or maximize. Specific wording helps SMTO build a request with details the Desktop skill accepts.
  2. If you want a file opened in an app, give the file's full location on the Gateway computer, starting from the top folder or drive, and make sure the file exists there. The Desktop skill only opens files that already exist at a full location on that computer.
  3. Don't ask the Desktop skill to shut down or restart the computer, delete files, or run commands. To end a program, ask SMTO to end that program by name. SMTO refuses to open system tools such as shutdown, rm or kill through the Desktop skill.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the desktop action, or tells you plainly that the app or window couldn't be found.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the exact request you typed, to the person who manages SMTO. Mention which app, window or file you meant.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Desktop request validation rejected an unknown operation, arguments that failed the operation schema or integer/finite checks, a non-absolute or missing file operand, or a blocked launch target (for example shutdown, rm or kill).

What this means

  • Desktop validation rejected an unknown operation, invalid typed/bounded arguments, nonfinite values, invalid local file input or a prohibited launch target. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Desktop validation rejected an unknown operation, invalid typed/bounded arguments, nonfinite values, invalid local file input or a prohibited launch target.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the operation with its advertised schema and target-local identities/paths; do not convert it into arbitrary command arguments.

How to fix it

  • Compare the tool call with the operation's schema in src/gateway_core/desktop_contract.py (SPECS): use only listed fields, integer pid/offset/limit/geometry values, finite numbers, and current window_id and process_identity values. launch_application files must be existing absolute paths, system administration programs are refused, and commands, argv and environment variables are never accepted.
  • Use the advertised structured schema, bounded values and current target-local identities. Commands, argv and environments are not accepted.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the advertised structured schema, bounded values and current target-local identities. Commands, argv and environments are not accepted.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid authorized structured request is admitted for the exact intended desktop target.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
